newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong stocks move ahead in morning trade.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong stocks move ahead in morning trade.

text.p: Hong Kong stocks moved higher in Monday morning trade after taking a hit last week, but analysts said investors were still cautious and the upside this session was likely to be limited.
The Hang Seng index was up 84 points at 12,868. Turnover was HK$1.92 billion after the first hour of trade.

"I guess the favourable news is that the U.S. market has been stabilising but tomorrow there is the FOMC (Federal Open Market Committee) meeting so investors are a bit cautious," said Patrick Chia, research director at China Everbright Research.
The Dow industrials rose 1.16 to 6,304.87 points on Friday.

With the Christmas holiday approaching, analysts said the market was likely to settle down into a quiet trading pattern this week. "May be for the next two weeks the Hang Seng range will be around the 12,600 to 13,000 level," said Chia.

Geoff Galbraith, institutional sales trader at Nava SC Securities, said Hong Kong stocks were likely to take their cue from Wall Street. "I think Hong Kong is limited on the upside. I think it will kind of go sideways," he said.
He said the Hang Seng could rebound if Wall Street staged a convincing turnaround, but did not expect that to happen. The Hang Seng index fell 318.66 points, or 2.4 percent, last week.
H-shares failed to follow the rest of the market higher, with the sector index slumping 32.28 points to 905.71.
Analysts said China's comments this weekend that its soaring domestic stock markets were overheating had hurt the shares.
"If A-shares tumble then H-shares will be also affected," said Chia.
Shanghai's A-share index was down 115.091 points at 1,047.959 in morning trade and the B-share index was down 6.082 points at 60.209.
Guangdong Investment unit Guangdong Tannery made its debut on Monday. Its shares more than doubled at the start of trade, opening at HK$2.50 compared with an issue price of HK$1.03.
"I think it is in line with the IPO response. It is in line with Guangdong Investment's PER (price earnings ratio)," said Chia, adding that Guangdong Investment was trading at a PE of about 20 times.
Guangdong Tannery offered 110 million new shares, of which 30 million were offered for public subscription. The offering was 667 times subscribed.
Karrie International also made its market debut on Monday. Its shares opened at HK$1.40 compared with an issue price of HK$1.15 per share, but later slipped back to HK$1.16.
